newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: European Union gives Zimbabwe aid for rural poor.
newsitem.headline: European Union gives Zimbabwe aid for rural poor.

text.p: The European Union is to give Zimbabwe Z$1.5 billion (U.S.$140 million) over the next five years under an agreement largely aimed at helping the country's rural poor, Zimbabwean officials said on Friday.
Zimbabwean officials at the signing ceremony said the money would be disbursed under the recently concluded LOME IV Convention that benefits countries in the African, Caribbean and Pacific regions.
Zimbabwean acting Finance Minister Emmerson Mnangagwa said Harare would try to develop sound and practical programmes to help the poorer sections of its population.

"The programmable resources allocated to Zimbabwe will go for priority sectors of rural development, agriculture, social sectors of education and health via the micro projects programme, economic reform programme, investment and trade promotion and income generating projects," Mnangagwa said.
